title: Session 18 — Friction
rightsHolder: Jamey Phoenix Bethea, Conceptual Combat Academy

meta.probingQuestion: What does your friction do to the people across from you?
meta.connection: You can pin someone hard and still keep them safe. That is control of your own force. Your conflict off the mat lands on real people too, and the same control applies: honest friction, not harm.
meta.takeaway: Tonight you worked from an underhook tie, open guard, and a figure-four pin. You can hold someone hard and still keep them safe, and that control is yours to use on purpose. Your friction off the mat lands on real people too. You get to choose honest friction over harm.

slides.title: What does your friction do to the people across from you?

body.text: This is tripping him by blocking his foot.

items: The overhook player wins when the underhook player falls onto his own hips or hands.
The underhook player wins by closing his own hands under the overhook player's elbows.

body.text: This is knocking a standing man down, sitting.

items: The bottom player wins by standing up to grab the top player's hips, or by putting the top player's back on the mat and standing.
The top player wins by touching his shin to the bottom player's knees or body.

body.text: This is holding one arm with both hands.

items: The top player holds as long as he keeps the grip.
The bottom player wins by breaking the grip.

slides.title: What made it work?
slides.question: You've got a figure-four grip locked from under your partner's elbow. What's the smart move?

options.text: Keep the grip locked from under his elbow.
options.feedback: Holding it there is control without harm, honest friction instead of forcing something.

options.text: Slide the grip up onto his shoulder instead.
options.feedback: Sliding up loses the grip you already built.

options.text: Loosen the grip to let him breathe easier.
options.feedback: Loosening the grip gives the position away.
